analysis: Integration of four unit analyses. Changes: docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, new paragraph at head ~715-719 on Qwen 3.5 forced tool_choice), a changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen38-mtp-forced-tools.md), and ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift. In the Swift file, advertisesCapability (head ~line 75) now checks ModelRuntimeRequirements.qwen38ConcreteModelIDs.contains(model.id) instead of the single qwen38ConstrainedModelID (base line 18), so the embedded-MTP Qwen3.8-27B build can advertise forced tools. validateParser (head ~line 151) now treats model types with the prefix qwen3_5 as nativeQwen, accepting .qwen35 or .xmlFunction. Qwen35TemplateFix.applies and nativeStructuredTarget still gate forcedStrategy. Forced tool choice stays under structuredPostValidation (parse, function selection and schema validation before exposure), so it fails closed. Nemotron still rejects .qwen35 per the tests. Nothing touches encryption, keys, attestation, authorization, the prefix cache or wire protocol, so T-008, T-011, T-041, TB-002 and TB-007 are unaffected in the supplied evidence. Unverified contracts, recorded but not findings: the contents of ModelRuntimeRequirements.qwen38ConcreteModelIDs (defined outside the supplied files); whether the MTP ID shares the same M5/NAX runtime-capability filter at registration (CoordinatorClientCodec), since the tests only assert filtering for the legacy Qwen27 ID; and whether the qwen3_5 prefix also matches qwen3_5_moe and any other intended types. These affect only capability advertisement and tool-call correctness, which is availability and routing quality. No regressions are identified.
